name: Milton Keynes

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: only the national mandatory licence for HMOs with five or more people, not all related, sharing facilities. An Article 4 direction controls new small HMOs through planning in parts of the city.
licensing.fee: £730 for a new or renewed HMO licence (£485 on application and £245 on approval)

neighbourhoods.name: Central Milton Keynes
neighbourhoods.housing: Apartment blocks and new towers around the shopping centre and station, largely privately rented.

neighbourhoods.name: Bletchley
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and inter-war terraces in the old town, with post-war estates around it.

neighbourhoods.name: Wolverton
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian railway-workers' terraces in a grid of streets, many privately rented.

neighbourhoods.name: Fishermead and Netherfield
neighbourhoods.housing: 1970s new-town estates of terraced houses and flats.

neighbourhoods.name: Stony Stratford
neighbourhoods.housing: Georgian and older coaching-town buildings on the High Street, with later estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Broughton and Brooklands
neighbourhoods.housing: Large estates of new-build houses and flats on the city's eastern flank.

neighbourhoods.name: Newport Pagnell
neighbourhoods.housing: A market town of older terraces and cottages, with post-war and new estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Olney
neighbourhoods.housing: Stone-built Georgian and older town houses and cottages, with newer estates.

housing: Milton Keynes mixes the 1970s and 1980s new-town grid estates, older towns such as Bletchley, Wolverton, Stony Stratford and Newport Pagnell, and large new-build districts still being built on the edges. About one in five households rent privately, with many lets in Central Milton Keynes apartments, new-town terraces and the Victorian streets of Wolverton and Bletchley. Rural villages to the north have stone cottages and farmhouses.
checkinTips: 1970s new-town estates in Fishermead, Netherfield and Beanhill: photograph flat roofs, timber cladding, windows and any condensation or mould.
New-build homes in Broughton, Brooklands and the western expansion areas: record snagging marks, sealant and any cracks so they are noted before the tenancy.
Central Milton Keynes apartments: note fob, key, parking and bike store counts, and photograph balconies and the intercom.
Victorian terraces in Wolverton and Bletchley: photograph the rear yard, alley access, gutters and any damp in back rooms.
Stone cottages in Olney and the northern villages: record damp patches, wood burners and flues, and any oil tank.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact Milton Keynes City Council's Private Sector Housing team, which can inspect homes and take enforcement action.
